name: nygel

attributes.attribute: dunked its rider in the sea
less dangerous than the Water Horse
streams from the old grain and woolen mills
wrecked mills left on at night

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: On the Shetland Isles a water-horse went by the name nygel or nuggle. Its common dress was a gentle gray pony shown to passersby. A rider who climbed up found himself carried to the sea and ducked in the waves. That bath proved far milder than a swim with the true Water Horse. The being had a fondness for the millraces that fed the old grain and wool wheels. Leave a wheel turning through the night and its mood fell sour. The nygel then shored the shaft and tore at the mill's guts. Even so it stayed a fair deal kinder than the Nuckelavee.

okr.objective: Portray the nygel, a gentler kelpie that shored and briefly bathed its riders.
key_results: It bound its rider in the pony and ducked him in the surf.
That ducking proved less than a full death at sea.
It took the millraces and wrecked a wheel, left turning after dark.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
